input.quote: the amount of any other actual direct damages, up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services.
input.rationale: The cap itself is acceptable: Sections 9.1 and 9.2 are drafted symmetrically (greater of $100,000 or twelve months' charges paid, both measured on Customer's charges to IBM), indemnification payments and bodily injury/property damage sit outside the cap in each direction, and Section 10 excludes consequential damages mutually. That satisfies the fallback cap basis and mutuality. However, the carve-outs fall short of the fallback, which requires at least indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct: only indemnities are carved out, and Section 6 expressly makes Sections 5, 9 and 10 prevail over the confidentiality agreement for information in the hosting environment, so confidentiality (and any data/security) breaches are pulled inside the cap, with no exclusion for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement. We therefore added a single mutual "Excluded Claims" sentence as new Section 9.3 rather than reopening the cap. Noted but not separately flagged: Section 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM liability for loss of Customer records or data one-sidedly, which the new carve-out partially addresses where such loss results from breach of security/confidentiality obligations or wilful misconduct.

proposal.summary: Add mutual uncapped carve-outs (Excluded Claims) to the Section 9 liability caps
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The caps in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 are mutual and set at twelve months' charges, which works for us, but they currently capture breaches of confidentiality (expressly, via Section 6), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. We have added a short mutual carve-out sentence so those Excluded Claims, together with the indemnities, sit outside the cap for both parties.

ops.text: 9.3 Excluded Claims. Notwithstanding Sections 9.1 and 9.2 and the final sentence of Section 6, the limitations and exclusions in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 do not apply to, and neither party's liability is limited for, Excluded Claims. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations under Section 8, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.
